title: Designing type-safe component APIs
description: Learn how to design React component props that are easy to use, hard to misuse, and fully type-safe.

data.text: A component API is the contract between the component and every developer who uses it. If that contract is weak, bugs appear in consumer code, documentation becomes unclear, and refactors become risky. TypeScript lets you design APIs that guide developers toward correct usage.

The best type-safe APIs prevent invalid prop combinations before they reach the component. Instead of passing booleans that conflict with each other, use a discriminated union to make each state explicit.

data.title: Preventing Invalid Prop Combinations
data.content: Using a union instead of multiple booleans

data.text: Polymorphic components accept an `as` prop that changes the rendered element. This pattern is common in design systems. The challenge is making the component props change based on the element type while keeping the API discoverable.

data.title: Polymorphic Component with as Prop
data.content: Rendering as different HTML elements safely

data.text: Compound components share state through context while letting consumers arrange the pieces freely. TypeScript can infer the child component types so consumers get autocomplete and compile-time validation.

data.title: Type-Safe Compound Components
Design for Discoverability
data.text: The best component APIs are self-documenting. Use descriptive prop names, provide sensible defaults, and let TypeScript infer types where possible so consumers can focus on behavior instead of configuration.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use discriminated unions instead of conflicting booleans
Compound components share state through typed context
Make the common path the easiest path
data.takeaway: Type-safe component APIs reduce bugs, improve documentation, and make your design system easier to adopt.
